item.title: Faster Retrieval for Better, More Efficient RAG
item.description: Maximum inner product search (MIPS) sits at the core of recommendation systems, search, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). item.description: We present GHARP (Real-time Gaussian Head Animation from Large-scale Reconstruction Prior), a method that animates 3D human heads in real time from a few input images of a subject and a driving expression signal. item.title: Selection-Based Structured Reasoning: Toward Efficient Multimodal Search Agents
item.description: Multimodal agents commonly generate freeform reasoning before each action. item.title: Plan or Retrieve First? A Scale Study of Tool Discovery Architectures
item.description: Tool-augmented LLM agents discover relevant APIs from large registries before planning execution, yet finite context windows prohibit injecting all tool definitions into a single prompt. The dominant approach, which we term Retrieve-then-Plan (RtP), embeds the user query and retrieves similar tools via approximate nearest-neighbor search. item.title: Code-Switching Detection via Language-Selective Dimensions in Speech Foundation Models
item.description: Code-switching (CS), the alternation between languages within an utterance, is common in multilingual speech but underrepresented in pretraining corpora. item.title: The Design Space of Tri-Modal Masked Diffusion Models
item.description: Discrete diffusion models have emerged as strong alternatives to autoregressive language models, with recent work initializing and finetuning a base unimodal model for bi-modal generation. item.title: Mix, Don't Tune: Bilingual Pre-Training Outperforms Hyperparameter Search in Data-Constrained Settings
item.description: For most languages of the world, language model pre-training operates in a data-constrained regime where models must repeat their training data many times, degrading generalization. item.title: Large Language Models for Machine Translation Quality Annotation: Humans and Models Are Both Challenged
item.description: Large Language Models (LLMs) are considered to be a more efficient and cost-effective alternative to human judgment for Machine Translation (MT) evaluation.
